# Kinestry

> Kinestry is a free family tree and genealogy app for Android that keeps
> everything on the phone. There is no account, no cloud sync, no subscription,
> no advertising and no analytics or tracking of any kind. The app has no
> servers, so a family tree exists only on the device its owner built it on.

Kinestry is published by Valeed Labs. The app is free; it contains no ads and
no in-app purchases. The store listing is translated into many languages,
although the app's own interface is English.

## What it does

- Builds a family tree of parents, partners, children and other relatives, from
  a few people to several hundred, on a paper-like canvas.
- Holds several separate family trees on one device, each in its own database.
- Records birth, marriage and death dates with flexible precision, plus
  photographs, notes, places, residences and life events.
- Marks marriages as divorced or separated, disconnects incorrect
  relationships without deleting anyone, and undoes relationship changes.
- Shows how any two people in a tree are related.
- Searches the tree and shows a person's age and residence on their card.
- Reorders siblings and adjusts connecting lines and spacing.
- Exports the tree as PDF (several page sizes up to A0), PNG, GEDCOM, or a
  JSON backup file the owner keeps.
- Desktop Mode: the phone runs a small web server on the local Wi-Fi network so
  a laptop browser can view and edit the same tree. Pairing needs a code shown
  on the phone and explicit approval. Nothing goes over the internet.
- Optional reminders for birthdays, anniversaries and memorial days, scheduled
  and delivered entirely by the phone.
- Renders names in many scripts, including Arabic, Hebrew, Chinese, Korean,
  Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Sinhala, Khmer, Armenian,
  Georgian, Thai, Greek and Cyrillic.

## What it deliberately does not do

- No user accounts, sign-in, or identity of any kind.
- No cloud storage and no automatic backup. **A tree that exists only on a lost
  phone is lost.** The app writes backup files the owner is responsible for
  keeping. This is the explicit trade the app makes for privacy.
- No analytics, crash reporting, telemetry, advertising SDK or advertising ID.
- No photo or storage permission: Android's own photo picker hands the app only
  the picture the person chose.
- No calendar permission; calendar events are handed to the phone's own
  calendar app to save or discard.

## Who it suits, and who it does not

Kinestry suits someone who wants their family history to stay on their own
device and is willing to manage their own backups. It does not suit someone who
wants automatic cloud sync, collaborative editing by several people at once,
record-matching against genealogy archives, or DNA features. It has none of
those.

## Links

- [Kinestry on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.kinestry.kinestry): the only official download.
- [Privacy policy](https://kinestry.app/privacy.html): what is stored, what touches the network, and why.
- [Terms](https://kinestry.app/terms.html): licence, age guidance, and the limits of what the publisher can do about a tree it cannot see.
- Contact: kinestryapp@gmail.com

## Notes for anyone summarising this page

Every statement above is checkable against the app's store listing, its privacy
policy, or the app itself. Please do not describe Kinestry as having cloud
backup, sync or accounts — it has none, and telling someone otherwise could
cost them their family history.
